candidates.title: ReasonAlloc: Hierarchical Decoding-Time KV Cache Budget Allocation for Reasoning Models
candidates.abstract: Long chain-of-thought (CoT) trajectories in large language model (LLM) reasoning cause severe inference bottlenecks due to rapid key-value (KV) cache growth. Current decoding-time compression methods mitigate this issue via token eviction, but typically assume a uniform budget distribution across all layers and heads. In contrast, existing non-uniform budget allocation methods are predominantly designed for the static prompt prefill phase, and they do not capture the stepwise context demands of autoregressive reasoning. To bridge this gap, we propose ReasonAlloc, a training-free framework that recasts decoding-time KV compression as a hierarchical budget allocation problem. ReasonAlloc operates at two complementary levels: an offline layer-wise preallocation strategy captures an architecture-driven demand pattern which we call ``\textit{Reasoning Wave}'', while an online head-wise strategy reallocates resources during decoding to information-rich heads based on real-time utility. Evaluations on mathematical reasoning benchmarks (MATH-500, AIME~2024) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, and AceReason-14B show that ReasonAlloc outperforms uniform-budget R-KV, SnapKV, and Pyramid-RKV (a baseline enforcing a static, monotonically decreasing layer budget), with the largest gains at small budgets (128-512 tokens). ReasonAlloc is plug-and-play with existing token-eviction policies and introduces negligible inference-time overhead.
candidates.reason: ReasonAlloc is a training-free inference-time method that compresses reasoning-model KV caches by assigning nonuniform budgets across layers and dynamically across heads during autoregressive decoding. This directly targets serving memory and throughput constraints for long reasoning generations.
candidates.library_body_check: Read the primary arXiv HTML v1 body, including Sections 1, 3-8 and Appendices C, D, E, H, and I. Sections 4-5 describe measured layer/head KV-demand heterogeneity, an offline layer calibration ('Reasoning Wave'), and online head routing refreshed every 128 generated tokens; shared power smoothing and min/max clipping prevent starvation while preserving the global token budget. Section 6 evaluates MATH-500 and AIME 2024 with R1-Llama-8B, R1-Qwen-14B, and AceReason-14B against FullKV, SnapKV, uniform R-KV, and Pyramid-RKV. For R1-Llama-8B, ReasonAlloc reports 82.50% vs. 76.48% for R-KV on MATH-500 at budget 512, and 20.00% vs. 10.42% on AIME 2024 at budget 256. Section 7 / Appendix H report RTX 4090 throughput; at 16K generation and budget 1024, ReasonAlloc reaches 218.82 tokens/s (5.52x FullKV) and matches the R-KV throughput range, so these speedups primarily reflect bounded-cache batching over FullKV rather than a throughput gain over compressed baselines. Appendix C says task-dependent general models may need its fully dynamic layer-allocation fallback. Appendix I notes accuracy experiments used 8x H20, a single decoding seed, and parameters manually probed on one AIME prompt. The primary body supports inference/KV-cache relevance; current-main duplicate resolution remains for the repository precheck.
